newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cabinet backs ending perpetual leases.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cabinet backs ending perpetual leases.

text.p: The Egyptian cabinet on Thursday backed a court ruling ending perpetual shop leases and said tenants could pass on the lease to just one generation of heirs, government televison said.

The announcement appeared aimed at appeasing shop tenants who were angered by a Constitutional Court ruling last month that abolished a clause that allowed them to pass on the lease to their heirs forever.

The cabinet's bill allows the heirs of non-residential sites to keep the lease until their death, after which the business relationship with the owner will be subject to civil law, the television quoted Minister of Cabinet Affairs Talaat Hammad as saying.
"The bill is designed to deal with the effects of the constitutional court's ruling," Hammad said after the cabinet meeting.
The bill still has to go for approval to parliament, which is dominated by the ruling National Democratic Party.
The February ruling gave real estate owners for the first time in decades recourse in the court to prevent leases from being automatically passed on to a tenant's heirs.
Shop tenants described it as irresponsible and said it would hurt them economically.
Egypt is seeking to shed the policies of the 1960s socialist era as part of its economic reform programme.

But the government had been trying for years to issue a new socially-sensitive law replacing the one governing ties between real estate owners and tenants, which was based on strict rent control and perpetual leases.
The current housing laws discourage investors from building, which results in housing and business space shortages and unaffordable rents.
